statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of seven representative public/unauthenticated paths. Logged-in reading, payment, cancellation, and account-management states were not entered because no test account or payment authorization was supplied; checks were judged only against exposed public surfaces.

page.framework: Next.js landing pages plus server-rendered legacy/document surfaces
page.notes: Public document marketplace and reader. Representative coverage includes landing, listing, document, upload, signup, 404 recovery, and an advertised locale target.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark preference matched but root color-scheme remained normal and the primary dialog stayed light.
The emulated preference matched and document.getAnimations() returned no active animations.
Text, links, form controls, and focus outlines remained visible in the forced-colors/high-contrast capture.

checkOutcomes.method: cross-document transition video and CSS/runtime probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The route capture shows a direct swap and no authored view-transition rule was detected.
No scroll-linked decorative effect or main-thread scroll animation was present; ordinary page/document scrolling remained native.

checkOutcomes.method: mobile layout and document-reader visual inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The covered surfaces use native scrolling and platform controls; no custom pointer-driven gesture that fights scrolling was observed.
Persistent header/search and the reader toolbar/page controls keep navigation context visible across long surfaces.
No tooltip, edge menu, or transient popover requiring anchor positioning was exposed in the covered unauthenticated states; the only open overlay was the viewport-fixed consent modal.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, edge menu, or transient popover requiring anchor positioning was exposed in the covered unauthenticated states; the only open overlay was the viewport-fixed consent modal.

checkOutcomes.method: screenshots of listing, reader and 404 journey
checkOutcomes.evidence: Category headings, reader page controls, and recovery links make location and the next destination apparent.

checkOutcomes.method: first-load screenshots at desktop and mobile
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent dialog obscures most or all first-load content.

checkOutcomes.method: dialog DOM semantics and keyboard probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent overlay is labelled role=dialog/aria-modal and exposes close, save, accept, and reject controls with visible focus.
The document reader gives the majority of its central viewport to the document; chrome remains compact and task-related.

checkOutcomes.method: layout metrics at 360x800 on landing and document templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Both mobile captures reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 with 0px horizontal overflow and a viewport meta tag.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS rule inventory and mobile layout
checkOutcomes.evidence: No container query rules were detected although viewport reflow works.
Several actions computed outline-style none and some targets were below 44×44 CSS pixels.

checkOutcomes.method: first-viewport screenshots across home, document, upload and signup
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headings and primary controls clearly identify explore/search, read/download, contribute/upload, and create-account purposes.

checkOutcomes.method: public discovery-to-reader walkthrough and signup form inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: A category exposes real document hrefs and the selected public document opens in the reader; signup exposes labelled email/password and federated paths. Account-only purchase/download completion was outside the unauthenticated public scope.
Native form validity returns actionable messages, polite/assertive live regions exist, and the 404 names the error and links back home/content.
Lighthouse LCP was 18.6s and TBT 650ms; the separate trace LCP was 1.90s with 76ms TBT, indicating variable but unacceptable cold-load evidence.

checkOutcomes.method: mobile CLS observers on landing and document templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Observed CLS was 0 on home and 0.0011 on the document, with image dimensions present.
Lighthouse TBT was 650ms; the separate trace recorded one 126ms long task.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against script DOM attributes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page transferred 2.85MB, including 2.13MB script; HTML was uncompressed and one head script was synchronous.
Lighthouse estimated 905KiB unused JavaScript and 28KiB unused CSS.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audit and axe corroboration
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found category card label/content mismatches; axe found no additional violations.

checkOutcomes.method: axe and Lighthouse accessibility plus forced-colors screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe found no violations, Lighthouse scored accessibility 1.0, and essential UI remained visible in forced colors.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse semantics and keyboard computed-style probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Category accessible-name mismatches and multiple controls with outline-style none prevent a fully reliable focus/name experience.
Body and heading copy uses readable sizing, spacing and wrapping without clipping across covered screenshots.
Reflow succeeds without overflow, but the menu control is 24×40px and consent checkbox boxes are 16×16px. No required media-caption case was present.
Lighthouse errors-in-console scored 1 with no recorded items.
The page uses HTML doctype, UTF-8, correctly proportioned/dimensioned modern-format images, and Lighthouse aspect-ratio audits passed.
Deprecation, BFCache, geolocation/notification-on-load, paste prevention, and source-map audits all scored as passing; security findings are recorded under the dedicated security principle.
The homepage has a descriptive title and meta description.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO and DOM link inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: Links are crawlable and viewport metadata is present, but Lighthouse found two generic Learn more links.
The public page returns 200, declares a canonical, exposes hreflang links, and robots.txt points to locale-specific sitemap indexes without blocking ordinary indexing.
The homepage exposes WebSite SearchAction and Organization JSON-LD plus matching og:title, og:description, and og:site_name.
HTTPS/HSTS and no exposed secrets pass, but CSP, nosniff and cookie hardening are incomplete.
69/72 requests and 2.46MB were non-www origins; five known trackers were active.
No permission prompt occurred on load, but signup offered no passkey/WebAuthn path.
HSTS is present, but CSP/frame protection, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and narrow cookie posture are incomplete.

checkOutcomes.method: raw HTML vs rendered discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw HTML returned 200 with 100% rendered-content word coverage, the H1 and description present, and no empty JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: mobile layouts, consent dialog, and 404 exercise
checkOutcomes.evidence: Covered overlays stay within the viewport with scrolling, mobile templates do not overflow, and navigation failures resolve to a recoverable 404.

The public website is a server-rendered, network-dependent document marketplace with native apps promoted separately; an offline/installable web-app promise is not part of the covered public experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public website is a server-rendered, network-dependent document marketplace with native apps promoted separately; an offline/installable web-app promise is not part of the covered public experience.

checkOutcomes.evidence: An unknown route produces a clear Page not found state, explanation, home/content recovery links, and no broken shell.

checkOutcomes.method: hreflang and explicit locale navigation probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The advertised Spanish URL delivered English lang/content at the www URL.

checkOutcomes.method: explicit Spanish locale navigation and locale metadata probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The explicit Spanish target did not preserve the requested locale, so locale-aware delivery could not be established even though hreflang variants are advertised.
The covered public landing, listing, document, upload, and signup surfaces expose no events, schedules, or user-facing times for which time-zone or DST handling applies.
checkOutcomes.reason: The covered public landing, listing, document, upload, and signup surfaces expose no events, schedules, or user-facing times for which time-zone or DST handling applies.

checkOutcomes.evidence: All optional advertising/personalisation purposes are checked by default, though a reject-all action is present.
Empty required fields produce browser-native messages, with dedicated polite/assertive live regions for email and password feedback.
Email and password are labelled, required, and use autocomplete=email/new-password; newsletter consent is optional and unchecked.

The public account entry clearly states one subscription for Scribd and Slideshare, offers multiple sign-up methods, and leaves marketing consent off; no sensitive account action was available without authentication.
33/36 images had no srcset and two were oversized, despite modern formats and dimensions.
Initial load fetches large payment, survey, social and duplicate analytics bundles that are not needed for first content.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR byte attribution and tracker inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: Third-party origins consumed 2.46MB, including 858KB from Google Tag Manager.

checkOutcomes.method: agent feature probe and robots policy
checkOutcomes.evidence: No WebMCP/agentic tools were present and robots explicitly blocks several major AI crawlers.

checkOutcomes.method: feature inventory and emerging-feature applicability judgement
checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-facing summarisation or generative feature is offered in the covered public UI, so built-in on-device inference has no current task to enhance.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-facing summarisation or generative feature is offered in the covered public UI, so built-in on-device inference has no current task to enhance.

checkOutcomes.method: baseline and post heap summaries around 10 reader scroll cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap self-size changed from 58.29MB to 59.11MB (+1.4%) and nodes from 1,058,563 to 1,069,632 (+1.0%); across isolated captures this is small enough not to establish unbounded retained growth.
The two-page reader baseline had 1.06M heap nodes and 58.3MB self-size; post-scroll remained similarly large.

Neither summary surfaced Detached* constructors among the largest retained constructor groups, and repeated scrolling did not produce a large population jump; intentional caches and isolated-run noise limit confidence.

paths.description: Public landing page, global navigation, consent, search entry, trial proposition, and site-wide metadata.
Technology & Engineering listing, representing category/listing templates and document discovery.
Public document detail/reader, representing Scribd’s primary content-consumption journey.
Public document-upload landing surface, representing contribution intent before authentication.
Account creation surface, representing the public authentication/form journey. No account was created and CAPTCHA was not bypassed.
Deliberately invalid URL, representing HTTP/navigation recovery.
Spanish hreflang target, representing locale routing and translated delivery.

findings.summary: The consent experience obscures the page on first load, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: Load screenshots show the consent dialog covering essentially the entire 360×800 viewport and more than half of the desktop viewport before users can engage with Scribd content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving first layer with equally prominent accept/reject actions; move partner-level controls into an explicitly opened preference dialog and preserve semantic light-dismiss where regulation permits.

findings.summary: The site does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reports color-scheme: normal and the consent surface remains rgb(255,255,254) with dark text; the screenshot remains a light-themed UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces, text, controls, and the consent UI through theme tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cross-page navigation swaps views without an authored View Transition.
findings.evidence: The 5-second home-to-category capture shows a direct document swap; probes found no authored view-transition rules even though the browser exposes document.startViewTransition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for same-origin MPA navigation and name only stable shared elements, with a reduced-motion-safe fallback.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-driven rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no container query rules, although the mobile layout itself reflows without horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable search, card, navigation, and consent components containment and use @container for local layout changes while retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Several controls have weak keyboard focus indication or undersized touch geometry.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found many actionable elements with outline-style none, including search and navigation controls; the mobile menu control measured 24×40px and consent checkboxes measured 16×16px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring for every control and make each pointer target at least 44×44 CSS pixels without shrinking the visual design.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is far outside the good user-experience range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 18.6s, FCP 6.6s, TTI 19.8s, TBT 650ms, and a performance score of 0.41. A separate trace was much faster (LCP 1.90s), showing substantial run/network variance but confirming at least one 126ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP path, prioritize only the LCP asset, and delay non-critical product, survey, payment, and analytics code until interaction or idle time.

findings.summary: The critical network path includes excessive scripts and an uncompressed document response.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 72 requests and 2.85MB transferred; 32 scripts accounted for 2.13MB. The 386KB HTML response had no content encoding, and DOM inspection found one synchronous head script plus five unrestricted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress HTML, keep all non-critical scripts async/deferred, split route code, and defer survey/payment integrations and non-critical styles until needed.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a large amount of unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 905KiB of removable JavaScript, led by Stripe (176KB waste), application chunks, Survicate, and multiple tag-manager bundles; it also estimated 28KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load Stripe, surveys, and route-specific code only at the moment their feature is invoked, and consolidate tag-manager/analytics bootstraps.

findings.summary: Some category links expose accessible names that do not match their visible labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported label-content-name-mismatch for category cards, e.g. visible “Art / 6 categories / View all” with aria-label “View all categories in Art”.
findings.suggestedFix: Let the visible card text form the accessible name, or make the aria-label include the visible wording in the same order.

findings.summary: A small set of links uses generic text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO found two “Learn more” links with no destination context, despite the page otherwise using crawlable hrefs and a valid viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the destination topic in link text or its accessible name, such as “Learn more about copyright and DMCA”.

findings.summary: Important browser security policies and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking policy, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. One first-party stable-ID cookie lacked Secure, while another used SameSite=None with a 400-day lifetime. HSTS was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, add nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite and lifetime compatible with their purpose.

findings.summary: Third-party tracking and integration code dominates the initial load.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributed 69 of 72 requests and 2.46MB of 2.85MB transferred to non-www origins. The tracker probe found 16 external origins and five known tracker domains, while the UI advertises 53 IAB partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block optional integrations before consent, remove duplicate analytics tags, proxy or self-host essential assets where appropriate, and load payment/survey/social code only in context.

findings.summary: Public signup supports password and federated identity but exposes no passkey route.
findings.evidence: The signup DOM uses email + new-password and Google/Facebook/Apple providers; script inspection found no navigator.credentials, PublicKeyCredential, or WebAuthn integration. No permission prompts fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside federated methods, with password retained as a recovery-compatible fallback during rollout.

findings.summary: The advertised Spanish locale target resolves to English content in a fresh browser session.
findings.evidence: The homepage advertises hreflang=es at es.scribd.com, but navigating there ended at https://www.scribd.com/ with lang=en-US, an English title, and English H1/content.
findings.suggestedFix: Honor explicit locale URLs independently of browser/geolocation defaults, preserve canonical/hreflang reciprocity, and set lang/dir from the delivered translation.

findings.summary: Optional consent purposes are preselected by default.
findings.evidence: First-load screenshots show Storage, Targeted Advertising, Personalization, and Performance Cookies all checked. Reject Non-Essential is visible and comparable, but “Save Preferences” preserves the opt-in defaults unless users edit each purpose.
findings.suggestedFix: Default optional purposes to off and make consent an affirmative action; keep Reject Non-Essential as prominent and easy as Accept All.

findings.summary: Most images lack responsive source selection.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 33 of 36 images without srcset and two oversized images; formats and dimensions were otherwise modern and stable.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width-based srcset/sizes for hero and category artwork and serve only the resolution each rendered slot needs.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume a disproportionate share of page resources.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins transferred 2.46MB (86% of the load); Google Tag Manager alone transferred 858KB, before a user invoked payment, surveys, or social functionality.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level third-party budget, remove duplicate tags, and gate surveys, Stripe, social pixels, and advertising code behind user intent and consent.

findings.summary: Document capabilities are not exposed through structured agent tools, and several major AI crawlers are explicitly blocked.
findings.evidence: The document probe found no WebMCP or agentic tool registration. robots.txt disallows CCBot, Claude-Web, ClaudeBot, AI2Bot, and others, despite public document content having summarisation value.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent access matches product policy, expose tightly scoped read/search/summarise actions through agentic forms or WebMCP and document a deliberate crawler policy; keep upload, purchase, and account actions permission-gated.

findings.summary: The public two-page document viewer starts with a large JavaScript heap graph.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 1,058,563 heap nodes, 4,536,273 edges, and 58.3MB of self-size. Ten scroll-to-end/back cycles produced 59.1MB and 1,069,632 nodes, a small delta that does not itself prove a leak but leaves a heavy baseline for a two-page document.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the reader’s initial heap by constructor and retainers, lazy-create offscreen/recommendation UI, and unload document/page structures no longer needed.

findings.summary: Cold-load scripting blocks the main thread for too long.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 650ms Total Blocking Time; the independent trace recorded a 126ms long task and 76ms of blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break large startup work into prioritized tasks, defer non-critical integrations, and yield between hydration or initialization chunks.

taskList.title: Cut the cold-load LCP and unused JavaScript by intent-loading Stripe, surveys, social pixels, and analytics
Deploy CSP and complete browser security/cookie policies
Replace the full-screen, preselected consent wall with compact privacy-respecting defaults
Restore visible focus and 44×44 touch targets across header and consent controls
Honor explicit locale URLs and validate hreflang delivery
Add responsive image candidates and enforce a third-party/resource budget
Profile and reduce the document reader’s initial heap footprint
Add passkey support to account creation and sign-in
Add dark-theme tokens and color-scheme integration
Adopt container queries and cross-document View Transitions for reusable/navigation surfaces
Correct category accessible names and generic link text
Define a deliberate agent-access policy and structured read/search capabilities
